result:
Memo submitted. Here's the short version of what I found and what I couldn't finish.

**Flux result (US, Mar vs Feb, USD)** – three lines cleared both thresholds (>10% and >$5,000):

| Acct | Line | Feb | Mar | Δ$ | Δ% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5000 | Hosting & Infrastructure | 31,301.80 | 40,948.20 | +9,646.40 | +30.8% |
| 6300 | Travel | 785.40 | 7,158.41 | +6,373.01 | +811% |
| 6400 | Marketing Programs | 7,898.14 | 29,686.00 | +21,787.86 | +276% |

**5000 Hosting – driver identified.** Recurring Stackline production hosting is flat ($31,301.80 in Feb via JE-00125 → $31,148.20 in Mar via JE-00232). The whole variance is JE-00258, a $9,800 Stackline "one-time data migration" invoice (SC-M-2203) dated 3/14. It holds up as an explanation, with one caveat: I didn't get to open the underlying invoice, so I couldn't confirm the service period, that it's properly expensed vs. capitalized, or that it isn't also sitting in the 2100 accrual. Worth a two-minute look.

**6300 Travel and 6400 Marketing – drivers NOT verified.** I ran out of tool-call budget before I could pull the transaction detail on these two accounts. I did not invent drivers for them; the memo marks them as open and gives the reviewer the specific things to check (Travel/Training reclass given 6320 went to zero; the round $29,686 in Marketing suggests one or two large invoices or an accrual that could be a prepaid).

**Other things to know:**
- Depreciation shows $0 in March only because the "Record depreciation" checklist item is still open — not a real variance. Prepaid software amortization, payroll accrual, AP cutoff and bank recs are also still open, so this flux is preliminary and 5000/6400 in particular could still move.
- No journal entries posted, no exceptions flagged — nothing warranted either without the supporting detail.

If you re-run this with a fresh session, the two calls needed are `list_transactions` for US accounts 6300 and 6400 in 2026-03, plus opening the support doc behind JE-00258.
